I have farmed this land for many years. The soil here in the North West is sandy and tired, so I will buy one bag of the subsidized NPK fertilizer from the agro-dealer to help the millet. I also have goat and sheep manure that I will spread on the plot before planting. I keep my own millet seed from last season because it is hardy and I do not need to spend money on new seed. Weeding will take much of our time, but my family can manage the work on this small plot—we have no money to hire laborers. We depend entirely on the rains, and millet does not suffer badly from pests here, so I will not buy chemicals.
